documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: Sentry Sentry is a Webhook Validating Admission Controller that enforces rules cluster wide on objects in Kubernetes prior to admission.

documents.title: Rules
documents.text: Sentry currently supports the below enforcement rules. If they are not set in the config.yaml with "enabled" set to true, they will not be enforced. Each rule can ignore a set of namespaces. To enforce different configurations you can launch this admission controller under different names with different configurations.

documents.title: Limits
documents.text: Limits will ensure all pods have limits for cpu and memory set and are within the range you provide.

documents.title: Source
documents.text: Source ensures images are only pulled from allowed sources. This is a very simple string match. This will only check if your image string starts with strings provided in the config. To ensure your domain is not read as a subdomain, it is best to end your domain with a "/". By listing the entire image path with or without tag, you can allow specific images from a repository. So "gcr.io/google containers/pause-amd64" would only allow the pause container. Due to the matching strategy this also means "gcr.io/google containers/pause-amd64foo" would also pass.

documents.title: NsLabels
documents.text: NsLabels ensures all namespaces have labels, so you can enforce NetworkPolicies.

documents.title: Run
documents.text: This is the Beta release To run in your cluster, clone this respository, and edit manifest.yaml to suit your requirements. Then you can run Be Aware : Like PodSecurityPolicies and RBAC, these rules are powerful, and will banhammer ANY pods that violate the rules. You have been warned...

documents.title: Development
documents.text: To develop a new module, you can copy the example module. And then import it in the main.go Configuration is loaded using mapstructure. If you need have special decoding for your configuration you can register a decoder, please reference the limits module decoding hook in limits/config.go. You can add e2e tests by adding a folder for your module in test-manifests, and adding manifests named in the following convention. Anything not titled with "pass" as an "expectation" will be expected to fail. Then make sure your module is enabled in the manifest.yaml.
